results.evidence: WTA's hike description says that at the ridge top (2.7 mi, 6,200 ft) the last water can be obtained by a steep downhill side path. So water exists near the crest (the waypoint is right in substance) and the approach's claim that nothing exists above Mueller Creek is wrong; wording keeps it as not guaranteed.

results.fact: Waypoint elevations below the ridge crest
results.evidence: WTA puts the ridge top at 2.7 mi / 6,200 ft and says the trail gains about 3,000 ft in just over 2 miles, which does not settle the 6,300 ft ravine pin (it could be either an overstated ravine or a small drop). A trip report says the steep trail runs straight up to about 5,400 ft before entering meadows, which is consistent with the descent text's ~5,400 ft forest line; the approach's 6,200 ft point is where the last trees end on the crest, so the treeline wording is two landmarks rather than a clear conflict. No source gives the ravine's elevation, so the 6,300 ft pin is left unchanged.

The itinerary says 'best done June through October' while the season chip and seasonal guidance say July-September. Outside sources only give a broad May-October hiking window with variable early-season snow; no two sources state a Jul-Sep or Jun-Oct window for this route, so nothing was changed.

WTA gives 7.2 mi round trip and 3,800 ft of gain; a separate trail database gives about 11 km and ~1,200 m (3,937 ft) from the same Lower Maynard Burn start. Both are far above the 3,000-3,400 ft in the gear list, which is below even the net rise from 3,300 ft to 6,808 ft.
